text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- In contrast to the big four banks, small local banks are experiencing a boom in Denmark attracting new customers, opening new branches and signing up new employees to serve growing demand. The Danish Bankers' Association estimates that local banks have hired 500 new employees within the last five years, bringing their staff total up to 6,500 with the number of branches 40 up in 1996 at 668.

--- Insurance companies are expected to up premiums after the number of car thefts in Denmark increased by 18 percent in 1996 to total more than 41,000 compared to previous years with annual averages of up to 35,000.

--- Eight Christian organisations strongly reject the idea of church weddings for homosexuals in a letter to Denmark's bishops. Danish bishops are to decide in April on whether or not to permit church weddings for homosexuals in a country where the state allows them legal partnerships.

--- Danish shipping group A.P. Moeller has decided to order a further three of container ships from Denmark's biggest shipyard, Lindoevaerftet, on the central island of Funen, ensuring the yard's 3,000 employees work until 1999.

--- Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction, buyer of troubled shipyard Danyard in northern Denmark, is in economic difficulty after failing to take over NQEA Australia Pty Ltd, casting doubt on the company's upcoming takeover of the Danish yard.

--- Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen reckons that full employment is within reach in Denmark within a few years but the small Centre Democrat Party, a former coalition partner, does not believe that the government's present economic policies can succeed in abolishing unemployment. Unemployment is at around eight percent of the workforce at present in Denmark.
